mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm glad you're here. Have you ever noticed how certain memories seem to linger, not just in your thoughts, but in your very bones? Sometimes, pain and fear don’t just fade away—they settle in, shaping how we feel, act, and even how safe we are in our own skin. Together, we’re about to explore why that happens, and what it truly means to heal from deep wounds. Blending science, powerful stories, and groundbreaking research, Bessel van der Kolk’s work, The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma, invites us to see trauma through a new lens—one that connects the mind, the body, and everything in between. We’ll look at how trauma lingers in the body, not just as a memory, but as a lived experience that can touch every part of life: relationships, emotions, even our sense of who we are. But more than that, we’ll discover how understanding these hidden connections can open doors to hope and healing. By exploring the interplay of neuroscience, psychology, and compassionate therapies, we’ll find that reclaiming a sense of safety and wholeness is possible, no matter where we’re starting from. So, let’s take this journey together—one that just might change the way you understand yourself, and the world around you.
